tendinitis: Swelling (inflammation) of your tendon, often caused by overuse or strain. This can make movement painful.
hypertension: High blood pressure. This means your heart is working harder than it should to pump blood through your body.
gastroesophageal reflux: Acid reflux or heartburn. When stomach acid flows back into your food pipe, causing a burning sensation.
myocardial infarction: Heart attack. When blood flow to part of your heart is blocked, potentially damaging heart muscle.
cerebrovascular accident: Stroke. When blood supply to part of your brain is interrupted or reduced.
diabetes mellitus: High blood sugar condition. Your body either doesn't make enough insulin or can't use it properly.
pneumonia: Lung infection that causes inflammation and fluid buildup in air sacs, making breathing difficult.
osteoarthritis: Wear-and-tear arthritis. The protective cartilage in your joints breaks down over time, causing pain.
asthma: Breathing condition where your airways narrow and swell, making it hard to breathe.
migraine: Severe headache with throbbing pain, often on one side, sometimes with nausea and sensitivity to light.
anemia: Low red blood cell count. Your body doesn't have enough oxygen-carrying cells, causing fatigue.
bronchitis: Inflammation of the breathing tubes in your lungs, causing coughing and mucus.
dermatitis: Skin inflammation causing redness, itching, and sometimes swelling or blisters.
insomnia: Trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, affecting your daily functioning.
sprain: Stretched or torn ligament (tissue connecting bones). Usually happens when you twist a joint awkwardly.
